builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
summary: NAVE replaces a two-stage detector (boundary-proposal network plus post-processing parameter search) with a single Conformer using per-bin complex mean subtraction, a PCEN channel, a frequency-dynamic convolutional stem, and a duration-matched convolution kernel. The cost is a task-specific architecture and input pipeline tied to known call duration and frequency bands, plus per-class threshold tuning, with no reported latency or memory figures. It can fail on target events whose duration or frequency characteristics differ from the baked-in inductive biases, and the leave-one-site-out gains may not transfer to non-acoustic or non-Antarctic domains.
rationale: This is a domain-specific bioacoustic detection method, not a general LLM efficiency or agent technique, so it falls outside the reader's production decision space unless they build audio event detection systems.
technique: Normalized Conformer for whale call detection

claims.statement: NAVE replaces a two-stage detector (boundary-proposal network plus post-processing parameter search) with a single Conformer using per-bin complex mean subtraction, a PCEN channel, a frequency-dynamic convolutional stem, and a duration-matched convolution kernel. The cost is a task-specific architecture and input pipeline tied to known call duration and frequency bands, plus per-class threshold tuning, with no reported latency or memory figures. It can fail on target events whose duration or frequency characteristics differ from the baked-in inductive biases, and the leave-one-site-out gains may not transfer to non-acoustic or non-Antarctic domains.

A single NAVE model with a tuned per-class threshold exceeds the WhaleVAD-BPN baseline on BioDCASE 2026 Task 2 under leave-one-site-out cross-validation, without a boundary-proposal network or post-processing search; no numeric margin is reported in the abstract.
